title: Open subgroups of an absolute Galois group
statement: Let K be a field [def-pc-field-extension], K^sep a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], and G=Gal(K^sep/K) with its Krull topology. For every open subgroup H of G, the fixed field L=(K^sep)^H is a finite separable extension [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] of K, H=Gal(K^sep/L), and the transitive G-set G/H is finite and discrete continuous. Conversely, the stabilizer in G of a point in any finite transitive discrete continuous G-set is open and the fixed field of that stabilizer is finite separable over K.

source.place: Tag 03SF (finite etale objects under a Galois extension), and the finite Galois correspondence used in the proof of Tag 03QR

proof.text: Let H be open in G. Since K^sep/K is Galois, the fixed-field correspondence gives L=(K^sep)^H finite-dimensional over K, separable over K, and Gal(K^sep/L)=H. This is exactly the statement of [lem-exc-etale-open-subgroup-fixed-field-galois]. The same node applies to the stabilizer H of any finite transitive discrete continuous G-set, because continuity makes a point stabilizer open.

source.place: Tag 03QR, proof: each point has an open stabilizer; Tag 0BML, Theorem 9.22.4, finite subextensions correspond to open subgroups

proof.text: The quotient G/H is finite and discrete: G is a compact topological group in its Krull topology, and H is open, so [lem-exc-etale-open-subgroup-quotient-finite-discrete] gives both assertions. Thus the orbit G/H is a finite discrete continuous G-set.

source.place: Tag 03QR, proof: an orbit is G/H for an open stabilizer and hence is a finite discrete continuous G-set
